title: Find a counterexample to the maximal rank conjecture.
statement:
Find a counterexample to the maximal rank conjecture.

\textbf{\emph{Conjecture}} (Maximal Rank Conjecture)

Let $A\subseteq\mathbb C$ be the annulus $A = \{1<|w| < e | w \in \mathbb C \} $. Given $(M,\omega)$ $n$-dimensional compact K\"ahler manifold, $\varphi_0$ and $\varphi_1$ potentials, the geodesic on $M \times A$ is obtained as the weak limit of solutions to the family of degenerating complex Monge-Ampère equations
\begin{cases}
(\pi^*\omega + i \partial \overline \partial \Phi_\delta)^{n+1} = \delta (\pi^*\omega + i dw\wedge d\overline w)^{n+1} \\
\Phi_\delta|_{M\times \{ 0 \} }=\varphi_0 \\
\Phi_\delta|_{M\times \{ 1 \} }=\varphi_1.
\end{cases}
Then $(\pi^*\omega+i\partial \overline \partial \Phi_\delta)|_{M\times\{\mathrm{pt.}\}} \geq \varepsilon \omega$ for $\varepsilon >0$ independent of $\delta$.

title: Miscellaneous (problem 5)
statement:
For $X$ and $Y$ i.i.d.\ log-concave random variables, what is

$$
\max_{\lambda \in [0,1]} h(\sqrt{\lambda} X + \sqrt{1 - \lambda} Y)?
$$

We expect that the maximum is achieved at $\lambda = 1/2$.

It is known that this is not true without log-cavity. The counterexample is given by $X,Y$ with density $x^2 \phi(x)$ where $\phi(\cdot)$ is the standard Gaussian density, which is a bi-modal density. Another counterexample exists when $X$ and $Y$ are uniform on $[a,b] \cup [-b, -a]$. For certain choices of $a$ and $b$, the maximum is achieved at $\lambda$ arbitrarily close to $0$. 

We finally note that the Shepp-Olkin conjecture is relevant here. For parameters $p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_n \triangleq \underline{p}$, with random variable

$$
X(\underline{p}) = Y_1 + Y_2 + \ldots + Y_n, \quad \text{ where } \quad Y_i \text{ are independent Bern}(p_i).
$$

Then $H(X(\underline{p}))$ is concave in $\underline{p}$. The open question is whether $H(X(\underline{p}))$ iincreases in $\underline{p}$ for $\underline{p} \in [0, 1/2)^n$.

title: Question 2.9 — Fix a basis for Fn and let An−1⊂ Aut(Fn) be the copy of Aut(Fn−1) corre- sponding to the first n− 1 basis elements.
statement: Fix a basis for Fn and let An−1⊂ Aut(Fn) be the copy of Aut(Fn−1) corre- sponding to the first n− 1 basis elements. Let φ:Aut(Fn)→G be a homomorphism of groups. If φ(An−1) is finite, must the image of φ be finite? Note that the obvious analog of this question for GL( n, Z) has a positive answer and plays a role in the foundations of algebraic K-theory. A diﬀerent approach to establishing Property (T) was developed by Zuk [ 85]. He established a combinatorial criterion on the links of vertices in a simply connected G-complex which, if satisfied, implies that G has property (T): one must show that the smallest positive eigenvalue of the discrete Laplacian on links is suﬃciently large. One might hope to apply this criterion to one of the natural complexes on which Aut( Fn) and Out( Fn) act, such as the spine of Outer space. But David Fisher has pointed out to us that the results of Izeki and Natayani [ 55] (alternatively, Schoen and Wang – unpublished) imply that such a strategy cannot succeed.

title: Symplectic Floer homology and Nielsen fixed point theory for mapping classes
statement:
For any mapping class $g\in\Gamma=\pi_0(\operatorname{Diff}^+(M))$, there is a monotone representative $\phi\in\operatorname{Symp}^m(M,\omega)$, with respect to some $\phi$-invariant area form $\omega$, such that
\[
HF^*(\phi)=H_*(M_{\mathrm{id}},\partial M_{\mathrm{id}};\mathbb Z_2)\oplus \mathbb Z_2^{N(\phi|_{M\setminus M_{\mathrm{id}}})},
\]
where $M_{\mathrm{id}}$ denotes the union of the components of $M\setminus\operatorname{int}(U)$ on which $\phi$ restricts to the identity. If $\psi$ is a standard Thurston-canonical-form representative of $g$ and $\lambda$ is the largest stretching factor of the pseudo-Anosov pieces of $\psi$ (with $\lambda:=1$ if there are no pseudo-Anosov pieces), then
\[
F^\infty(g):=\operatorname{Growth}\bigl(\dim HF^*(\phi^n)\bigr)=\lambda=h(\psi)=\limsup_{n\to\infty}|N(\psi^n)|^{1/n}.
\]

title: Catalan's Mersenne conjecture
statement:

c_0 = 2, \qquad c_{n+1} = 2^{c_n} - 1 .

title: General exact upper-bound conjecture for cliques on surfaces
statement:
Let $\Sigma$ be a surface with Euler characteristic $\chi$, let $\omega$ be the largest integer such that $K_\omega$ embeds in $\Sigma$, and let $G$ be a graph embeddable in $\Sigma$. Write $|V(G)|$ for the number of vertices of $G$.

**General exact upper-bound conjecture.** Every graph $G$ embeddable in $\Sigma$ has at most

$$
8|V(G)|-4(7+\sqrt{49-24\chi})+2^{(7+\sqrt{49-24\chi})/2}
$$

cliques, with equality if and only if $K_\omega$ triangulates $\Sigma$ and $G$ is obtained from $K_\omega$ by repeatedly splitting triangles.

The preceding bound $8(|V(G)|-\omega)+2^\omega$ is reported to fail for several surfaces without complete-graph triangulations, motivating this formulation in terms of the Euler characteristic. The conjecture gives the proposed exact extremal value for all surfaces.

title: The non-flowerable coin graph extremal equality conjecture
statement:
For $n\in\mathbb{N}$, let a **non-flowerable collection** be a collection $\mathcal{C}$ of $n$ coins from which no flower, that is, no coin graph representation of a wheel graph, can be formed. NF(n)=\max\{NF(\mathcal{C}):\mathcal{C}\text{ is a non-flowerable collection of }n\text{ coins}\}.

**Non-flowerable extremal equality conjecture.** For every $n\in\mathbb{N}$,

$$
NF(n)=E_4(n)=\left\lfloor\frac{11}{4}n-6\right\rfloor.

title: PageRank singular-gap conjecture
statement:
Let $G$ be a directed graph with $d_{min}^{out}>0$. For a parameter $\alpha$ and associated PageRank random walk, let $\mathbf{R}$ be the probability transition matrix, given by

$$
\mathbf{R}=\frac{\alpha}{n-1}(\mathbf{J}-\mathbf{I})+(1-\alpha)\mathbf{P},
$$

where $\mathbf{J}$ is the all-one matrix and $\mathbf{P}$ is the transition matrix obtained by choosing an outgoing arc uniformly at random. **PageRank singular-gap conjecture.** There is a universal constant $k$ such that

$$
\sigma_2(\mathbf{I}-\mathbf{R})^{-1}\leq \frac{k}{\alpha}.
$$

The conjecture asserts that, like the spectral gap, the PageRank parameter controls the singular gap uniformly over all directed graphs with positive minimum out-degree. The authors note that examples based on Gambler's ruin imply $k\geq 1.65637$, while the general bound remains open.

title: Häggkvist's conjecture on compatible Hamilton cycles in Dirac graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a **Dirac graph**, meaning a graph on $n$ vertices with minimum degree at least $n/2$. Let $\mathcal{F}$ be an **incompatibility system** over $G$, consisting for each vertex $v$ of a family of unordered pairs of distinct edges incident with $v$; edges in one of these pairs are incompatible. The system is **1-bounded** if every edge incident with any vertex is incompatible with at most one other edge at that vertex. A Hamilton cycle is compatible with $\mathcal{F}$ if every pair of its edges is compatible.

**Häggkvist's conjecture.** For every 1-bounded incompatibility system $\mathcal{F}$ over a Dirac graph $G$, there exists a Hamilton cycle compatible with $\mathcal{F}$.

The paper presents this as a conjecture of Häggkvist from 1988 motivating its study. The supplied text gives no resolution status, so the conjecture is recorded as open.

title: The generalized Bogomolov–Gieseker conjecture for tilt-stable objects on threefolds
statement:
Let $X$ be a smooth projective threefold. Let $
u_{\omega,B}$ be the tilt slope on the tilted heart $\operatorname{Coh}^{\omega,B}(X)$, where $\omega$ is ample and $B$ is a real divisor class. An object $E\in\operatorname{Coh}^{\omega,B}(X)$ is $\nu_{\omega,B}$-semistable if it satisfies the tilt-stability condition with respect to this slope. **The generalized Bogomolov–Gieseker conjecture.** For any $\nu_{\omega,B}$-semistable object $E\in\operatorname{Coh}^{\omega,B}(X)$ satisfying $\nu_{\omega,B}(E)=0$, one has

$$
\operatorname{ch}_3^B(E)\leq \frac{\omega^2}{18}\operatorname{ch}_1^B(E).
$$

This conjecture is the main inequality needed to construct Bridgeland stability conditions on threefolds. It is known in several important cases, including the abelian and Calabi–Yau threefolds of abelian type treated in the paper, but is not known for arbitrary smooth projective threefolds.

title: The star conjecture for minimum von Neumann entropy of connected graphs
statement:
Let $G$ be a connected graph on $n$ vertices. Its scaled Laplacian is $\rho(G):=L(G)/\operatorname{tr}L(G)$, where $L(G)=D(G)-A(G)$, with $D(G)$ the diagonal degree matrix and $A(G)$ the adjacency matrix. The von Neumann entropy of $G$ is the Shannon entropy of the eigenvalues of $\rho(G)$, namely

$$
S(G)=-\sum_{i=1}^n\lambda_i\log_2\lambda_i.

title: Barát–Thomassen conjecture on tree edge-decompositions
statement:
Let $T$ be a tree, and let $G$ be a simple graph. A **$T$-edge-decomposition** is a decomposition of the edges of $G$ into isomorphic copies of $T$. The paper presents stronger quantitative results for graphs with sufficiently large minimum degree, while the general assertion concerns arbitrary simple graphs and remains the motivating conjecture here.

title: Nonvanishing Hankel determinants for a morphic sequence
statement:
Let \(\mu\) be the morphism
\[
1\mapsto 12,\qquad 2\mapsto 23,\qquad 3\mapsto 14,\qquad 4\mapsto 32,
\]
and let \(a=\mu^\omega(1)\) be the infinite sequence it generates. For \(n\ge 1\) and \(k\ge 0\), define
\[
H_{n,k}(a)=\det\bigl(a_{k+i+j}\bigr)_{0\le i,j<n}.
\]
Can one prove that \(H_{n,k}(a)\ne 0\) for every order \(n\) and every starting position \(k\)?
